identity.name: Abraham Lake
identity.region: David Thompson Country / Canadian Rockies front ranges, Alberta
identity.summary: Long, narrow Rockies front-range reservoir (~32 × 3.3 km) along the North Saskatchewan valley / Hwy 11. Strong days are driven by valley-channeled synoptic flow, mountain thermals, and orographic acceleration—not prairie lake-breeze. Famous for wind-scoured clear ice in winter (Windy Point).

dam.name: Bighorn Dam
dam.location: northeast / downstream end near Windy Point
dam.notes: Reservoir level rises through summer; beach width shrinks late season.

geometry.notes: Fetch is highly anisotropic: very long along-valley, short across-valley. Wave state and usable wind depend strongly on whether flow is aligned with the valley.

windRegime.directionNotes: Expect along-valley preference. West/southwest mountain-lee and Pacific-influenced flow often accelerates through the corridor; easterly/northeasterly return or drainage flows can also run the valley. Cross-valley winds are blocked/turbulent near walls. Local kiters report consistent thermal enhancement on suitable days. Exact best launch depends on which way the valley is flushing.

seasonality.spring: Frontal passages + snowmelt season; cold water; variable reservoir level.
seasonality.summer: Thermal + valley flow; kiters note relatively consistent wind; water very cold (glacial rock flour blue); beaches better early/mid summer before full pool.
seasonality.fall: Stronger synoptic gradients return; windy corridor days common.
seasonality.winter: Strong scouring winds keep ice clear at places like Windy Point; snowkite possible when ice safe—extreme wind chill and ice hazards.

windRegime.contrastToPigeonLake: Pigeon = prairie synoptic + weak lake breeze on a round basin. Abraham = mountain valley channeling + thermal/orographic on a long thin reservoir. Do not reuse Pigeon enhancer constants.

proxyPoints.description: Central basin cell for along-valley wind/wave estimates.
Toward Kootenay Plains / SW valley approach—background before full channeling.
Near Bighorn Dam / Windy Point—often accelerated; useful for NE-end conditions.
Use model winds at ~700–850 hPa / ridge height to detect mountain-wave / strong cross-barrier flow that may not match valley surface dir.

ridePoints.name: Windy Point / dam end
ridePoints.notes: Literally named for wind; common access/viewpoint. Expect acceleration and scouring. Confirm legal access and ice/water safety.

ridePoints.name: Hwy 11 mid-lake gravel/sand beaches
ridePoints.notes: Multiple informal pullouts along David Thompson Hwy. Early summer wider beaches; late summer higher pool. Cold water always.

ridePoints.name: Southern basin / Preacher's Point area (generic)
ridePoints.notes: Useful when valley flow is out of the NE. Treat pins as approximate—verify current access.

enhancerModel.description: Two stacked effects: (1) pressure-driven flow accelerated along the mountain valley (gap/venturi-like), (2) daytime heating of slopes/valley floor adding thermal component when sun and weak–moderate background align. Cross-valley synoptic wind may be redirected into along-valley surface flow.

rulesSeed.channelingSpeedupNotes: Multiply along-valley background by ~1.1–1.3 when models show flow aligned with valley and ridge winds are strong—SEED ONLY.
rulesSeed.notes: Thermal add-on may be larger than Pigeon Lake because of mountain slope heating, but gust factor and direction uncertainty are much higher. Calibrate with logger/rider reports.

enhancerModel.triggerLogic: If valley-aligned synoptic/ridge flow is present, apply channeling boost. If midday sun and not fully overcast, add modest thermal. If models disagree or flow is cross-valley, mark low confidence and expect turbulence near walls.

cloudSensitivity.notes: Cloud mainly hits the thermal piece. Strong valley-channeled synoptic days can still blow hard under cloud. Convective cells and mountain thunderstorms can produce dangerous outflow.

failureModes.description: Mountain corridor winds are often much gustier than prairie lakes; reports of very strong gusts. Beginner loft risk.
When upper flow crosses ridges, surface wind near walls can be holey, reversing, or rotor-like even if mid-lake looks OK.
32 km long: upwind end may be light while downwind end is nuking (or vice versa after a shift).
Glacial/reservoir water stays cold all season—serious immersion risk.
Rising summer pool reduces beach; late season launches change or disappear.
Fronts, cap cloud, and storms develop/arrive fast; limited cell service in places.
Wind-polished ice is slippery; dam-related ice irregularities; wind chill can be severe. Ice safety is never forecastable from wind alone.
Remote corridor; rescue logistics harder than urban prairie lakes.

stations.name: No dedicated public mid-lake buoy confirmed in profile research
stations.notes: Priority calibration gap. Consider portable logger at Windy Point or mid-hwy pullout.

nearbyReferences.description: HRDPS / HRDPS-continental / ECMWF / ICON at valley vs ridge levels; compare 10 m valley points to 700–850 hPa.
Nearest official observations are imperfect proxies—valley channeling can differ sharply over short distances.

riderReports.suggestedPrompt: Which end of the lake? Along-valley dir? Gusty vs steady? Thermal afternoon bump? Pool level / beach OK?

rideableThresholdsKt.notes: Gust factor often higher than Pigeon—raise beginner mins and emphasize gust spread in briefs.

steps: Fetch multi-model 10 m winds at mid-lake + SW/NE valley proxies
Fetch ridge-level wind to detect cross-barrier / wave risk
Classify: along-valley channeling vs cross-valley turbulent vs light thermal candidate
Apply channeling factor if aligned; add thermal if sun allows
Pick preferred lake end from along-valley direction
Inflate gust factor vs prairie defaults
Emit Forecast Object + caution-heavy rider brief

confidenceHeuristics.high: Models agree on along-valley dir/speed; ridge and valley consistent; clear synoptic driver
confidenceHeuristics.medium: Speed spread large or thermal-dependent; mild cross component
confidenceHeuristics.low: Cross-valley upper flow; frontal timing; convection; ice transition; no obs

dataSourcesSuggested: Optional future: local weather station at Windy Point
Pool level / TransAlta reservoir info for beachability
AGS or other bathymetry if wave maps desired (reservoir DEM may differ from natural lakes)
